threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still wait for the bus at the stop instead of diving into that dodgy kebab shop for a pint. Locals know that’s where the real action starts.
Caught a glimpse of a guy on the 59 bus last night, serenading the driver with classic soul tracks. He actually got a few chuckles, but I think the driver was secretly vibing.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I saw a guy selling homemade sausages out of his bike cart at 2 AM, while a group of kids played soccer in the street. Classic Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain can you find a club that doubles as a swimming pool during the day. The dance floors get steamy, literally!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: A true local knows the 14-Mission schedule by heart and can spot a tourist fumbling with the Clipper card machines from a mile away.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a full tuxedo get on the 47, looked like he was headed to a wedding. Just sat down, adjusted his bow tie, and checked his watch like it was all normal.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often think they can just stroll into a bar and order a café amb llet. Here, it's mostly called a 'café au lait' — you'll confuse the locals!

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their excitement over the weekend mercados, but missing the subtlety of the siesta hours that leave locals unfazed.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still don’t know it’s pronounced 'Hack-nee' and not 'Hack-knee'; the confused looks on your face are a dead giveaway.
Last night on the 63, a bloke serenaded the whole bus with a ukulele. Surprisingly decent! Only in Brixton, right?

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a family having a picnic on a playground while a street performer juggled fire nearby—it felt like the heart of Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain can you find a bar that still serves cocktails in mason jars, but it’s the live DJ spinning vinyl that really makes it unique.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local when they know to check BART status before leaving home, especially after a train overheats. It’s like second nature.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy calmly reading a novel while Muni was delayed for 20 mins because of a dog on the tracks. Only in SF do you see that level of zen.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Most tourists don't realize that the best pastries in Gràcia aren't from the fancy bakeries, but from the little corner shops where the old ladies still bake.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by the way they stare at the public transport maps like it’s a Picasso. Old hands have the route memorized.
